theory.intro: The angles $30^{\circ}$, $45^{\circ}$ and $60^{\circ}$ occur so often that their sine, cosine and tangent are worth knowing exactly, without a calculator. Each exact value comes from one of two special right-angled triangles, and the boundary angles $0^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$ complete the set.
facts: The **45°–45°–90°** triangle is half a unit square: both legs are $1$ and the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{2}$. From it, $\sin45^{\circ}=\cos45^{\circ}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $\tan45^{\circ}=1$.
The **30°–60°–90°** triangle is half an equilateral triangle of side $2$: the side opposite $30^{\circ}$ is $1$, the side opposite $60^{\circ}$ is $\sqrt{3}$, and the hypotenuse is $2$.
Leave these values as exact surds in the booklet form: write $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ and $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ **unrationalised**, not as $\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ or $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$.
$\tan90^{\circ}$ is **undefined**: as the angle approaches $90^{\circ}$ the adjacent side shrinks to $0$, so $\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}$ has no value.
To find an unknown side, pick the ratio that links the known side and the unknown side to the given angle, substitute its exact value, then solve.
steps: Choose the ratio linking the known and unknown sides
Substitute the exact value of the ratio

foundation.question_text: State the exact value of $\tan90^{\circ}$, or write that it is undefined.
foundation.solution_text:
$\tan90^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}$
At $90^{\circ}$ the adjacent side is $0$, and dividing by $0$ has no value.
$\tan90^{\circ}$ is undefined.

The angle $45^{\circ}$ has opposite $1$, adjacent $1$ and hypotenuse $\sqrt{2}$.
$\sin45^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{hyp}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\cos45^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{adj}}{\text{hyp}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
$\tan45^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}=\dfrac{1}{1}=1$

From the $30^{\circ}$ angle, the opposite is $1$, the adjacent is $\sqrt{3}$ and the hypotenuse is $2$.
$\sin30^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{hyp}}=\dfrac{1}{2}$
$\cos30^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{adj}}{\text{hyp}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$\tan30^{\circ}=\dfrac{\text{opp}}{\text{adj}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

development.solution_text:
From the $60^{\circ}$ angle, the opposite is $2\sqrt{3}$, the adjacent is $2$ and the hypotenuse is $4$.
$\sin60^{\circ}=\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{4}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$\cos60^{\circ}=\dfrac{2}{4}=\dfrac{1}{2}$
$\tan60^{\circ}=\dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{2}=\sqrt{3}$
